name: Venera 13
lastSignal: March 1, 1982 — lander transmitted for about 127 minutes
tagline: For just over two hours, a Soviet lander endured the crushing heat of Venus and sent back a view no one had seen before.
credit: Original editorial illustration created for the Left Behind archive.

beats.goal: Explore Venus’s atmosphere and surface using a flyby spacecraft and a lander equipped with cameras and scientific instruments.
beats.achieved: The lander returned colour panoramas and measurements of the Venusian surface. It also analysed soil composition and survived about 127 minutes on the surface, far beyond its planned operating time.
beats.ending: The extreme temperature and pressure of Venus eventually overwhelmed the lander. The flyby craft continued its own observations before its mission ended.
beats.now: The Venera 13 lander remains on Venus. It is inactive, exposed to an environment of roughly 465°C and crushing atmospheric pressure.
beats.learned: Venera 13 demonstrated that short-lived landers can return extraordinary data from one of the most hostile planetary surfaces.
